name: honey-adulteration
description: Binary screening for sugar-syrup adulteration from hyperspectral reflectance of a honey jar.

input_requirements.per_observation: one segmented, calibrated, pre-processed reflectance spectrum
input_requirements.capture: SOC-710 hyperspectral imager, 400-1000 nm, processed as in Phillips et al. (2021). Other cameras/pipelines are out of distribution.
input_requirements.aggregation: jar probability = mean of observation probabilities; threshold 0.5

dataset.title: Hyperspectral Imaging adulterated honey dataset
dataset.creators: Phillips, Coleman, Takano, Abdulla (University of Auckland)
dataset.obtained_from: https://github.com/Esmael-Ahmed12/Adulteration (adulteration.csv, data of Ahmed 2024, PLOS Digit Health 3(6):e0000536)

reliability.summary: On honey products it has never seen, jar-level balanced accuracy is 0.81 (71% of pure jars and 90% of adulterated jars classified correctly). Estimated from only 7 pure jars, so the uncertainty is large. Treat output as a weak screening signal only.

limitations: Only valid for spectra captured and processed like the Auckland dataset (same camera, calibration and segmentation).
Trained on 12 New Zealand honey products from 7 brands; only 7 products have pure (0 %) jars.
Adulterant is sugar syrup at 5-50 %; other adulterants were not studied.
Low concentrations (5-10 %) are the hardest to detect.
Decision support only - the laboratory's own adulteration test result is authoritative.
